prompt: Some people believe that unpaid community service should be a compulsory part of high school programmers (for example working for a charity, improving the neighborhood or teaching sports to younger children). To what extent do you agree or disagree).
essay:
Some people believe that unpaid community service should be a compulsory part of high school programmes. I agree with this view because volunteering can help students develop important life skills and prepare them for their future. However, schools should give students some choice in the type of community work they do.

Firstly, education should not be limited to academic subjects. Young people also need to develop soft skills such as teamwork, self-discipline and empathy. Community service gives students an opportunity to work with different people, help others and become more responsible. For example, students could organise charity events, improve their neighbourhood or teach sports to younger children. These activities teach them how to cooperate with others and understand the needs of people from different backgrounds. As a result, they may develop a strong work ethic and become more active members of society.

In addition to developing life skills, community work can help students with their future plans. Universities and employers often look for qualities that academic grades alone cannot show. Volunteering can demonstrate that a student is responsible, willing to take part in activities and able to work well with others. Therefore, this experience may help young people stand out when applying for university or their first job.

Admittedly, compulsory community service could reduce students' free time and put extra pressure on those who already have a heavy workload. However, this problem could be reduced if schools allowed students to choose suitable activities and required only a reasonable number of hours.

In conclusion, I believe unpaid community service should be part of high school education because it develops practical and interpersonal skills and can support students' future education and employment.
